finding: Late workflow callbacks can legitimately arrive after destructive cleanup, but worker-side Convex mutations still treat missing rows as fatal.
evidence: apps/engine-convex/convex/packages/worker.ts:871-907 throws if run/window rows are missing during projectProcessState
apps/engine-convex/convex/packages/worker.ts:1132-1135 throws if an attempt row is missing during recordLlmAttemptFinish
apps/engine-temporal/src/workflows.ts:283-289 performs a non-cancellable projectSnapshot on cancellation
implication: Destructive cleanup and late callback delivery are not currently compatible, so autonomous resets still generate hard Convex failures.

finding: The delete path is paged and can remove run-scoped artifacts or the run row itself without any callback-safe tombstone or acknowledged drain barrier.
evidence: apps/engine-convex/convex/domain/maintenance/danger.ts:347-499 deletes batches, payloads, observability rows, artifacts, attempts, and finally the run row
There is no corresponding worker-side grace condition or missing-row no-op in projectProcessState or recordLlmAttemptFinish
implication: Even a logically successful reset can still look noisy or broken if callbacks arrive during or after cleanup.

finding: The recurring local Convex dev error is specifically a window projection callback failure, which means the race is broader than V3 run reset helpers alone.
evidence: MCP failure logs and the agent-owned bun dev session repeatedly show packages/worker:projectProcessState -> Window run not found
The error recurs roughly every 100 seconds, which is consistent with an active workflow or late callback loop still attempting projection after the row is gone
implication: The fix belongs at the callback/worker contract layer, not only inside the run reset helpers.
